from: Mostly used in the 3rd person: mi sembra = I think, it seems to me. sembrare + adjective: sembri stanco = you look tired.
to: Works like piacere when giving an opinion: the person is an indirect pronoun and the verb agrees with the thing: mi sembra giusto = it seems right to me, mi sembrano stanchi = they seem tired to me. Mi sembra che + congiuntivo = I think that. With a subject + adjective it is conjugated normally: sembri stanco = you look tired. Takes essere: mi è sembrata strana.
why: sembrare is a 'backwards' verb; note didn't explain the mi sembra / mi sembrano agreement
